docs.title: Ernie's website
docs.text:
Hello! I am Ernie. I am a UCSD student in the United States studying Mechanical Engineering. I am a international student from Taiwan. I am very interested in astronomy and rocket propulsion, and I wanted a space where I can share my discoveries and progress that I have made studying! I hope you will enjoy.

If you are interested in talking to me, my email is ernielin9494@gmail.com

docs.title: FRC Robotics team
docs.text: In high school I participated in my team's robotics program (3245, 2166) from 2022 to 2024.

This is our 2022 robot for the main team (3245), it features a fixed shooter and a ground intake, unfortunatly none of the mechanism worked and we ended up playing defence at the competitons

Here is a video of us testing the ground intake for our robot of the rookie team (our team version of cadets) (3166). The intake is using pneumatic actuators to deploy and retract. The intake ended up not functioning as effectivly as we liked but we still reached the World Championship after reaching the finals in the Utah Regional.

This was my first year at my robotics team, and I was tasked with building the drivebase alongside the mentor, the drivebase seen above ended up on the 3166 robot. Which is the robot that ended up at the World Championship.

I had not have much involvement in the 2023 season because my dad was sick and I had to go back to Taiwan for about a month. This made me miss almost all of the development cycle. Due to this I had only worked on miscellaneous parts on the robots, like tightening the chains on the arm mechanism.

This is our 2023 robot, note that the intake in this photo did not end up being the final version, as this is too heavy for the robot arm.

The robot has a elevator system, but we did not end up using the system, so we just bolted the elevator down instead. (our teacher was kinda mad that we wasted so much time building it)

This became our final robot for our first competition of the season, note that the intake has become smaller.

Here is footage of the competiton, we were the robot in the middle of the red side. As you can see we were too ambitions and the robot was not moving compared to our expectations. (appologies for the horrible videography)

We ended up with this new design inspired by one of the teams at our first competiton. Though our preformance was better, we did not fare better in our competition.

This is around the time I started learning how to CAD, this is one of the project I started, I studied the geometry of our intake and made a replica.

This was the last year of my high school, and this is when I decided that I needed to take ownership of one of the design project and I decided to work with my friend to design a climber for the robot.

This was our robot in action, as you can see, this year we switched to a swerve drivebase, which allowes our robot to move more freely.

This is me assembling the swerve drivetrain, since there was no need for pulleys/chains and since the motors are upright, it allowed more space to put the electrical component into the robot.

This was my prototype for the climber, it did not have other parts becaus it was supposed to be integrated to the main mechanism.

This is the protoype intergrated on the arm of the robot. The robot was able to use the slots to hold onto the chain and climb itself up using the arm. However we ended up scaping the project as the robot arm is a critical part of the robot and we cannot risk it being damaged. It is still fulfilling to be able to contribute to the design of the robot.

I had also decided to become the team's scout lead during competitions. I had wrote down notes of every robot in the competion, notes on most matches, as well as our win loss ratio. I had notes on every team as I walked around their pit area. This is the notes I wrote down on my own team. This is my impression on each robot during their practice matches and what their performance looks like on the field. I can use this data to refrence my notes I took on the robot in the pit area. This is our match statistic at the end of day one. We did end up as the 5th best team in the competition, and we reached finals in this competition.

docs.title: USS Hornet - Sea, Air and Space Museum
docs.text:
In Community College I volunteered at the USS Hornet for half a year, in the air restoration group.

At the start I helped on various project, I helped moved aircraft around, I detached drop tank from a F-86 Sabre, to working on a retired F-18. removing a droptank from F-28 Sabre to repaint Working on the F18

I decided that I want to work on the ongoing project to restore the Gemini space capsure, to remake the cockpit so that visitors can sit in it. The Gemini Capsule

We needed to add support beams before putting in the seats and the instruments.

You can see below that I grinded the inside of the capsure to expose the metal to prepare for welding.

I am ironman

Measuring the beam to make sure that they are level.

My first succesful tack weld!
